claim: Pergamon Museum is closed and will partially reopen June 4, 2027 with the Pergamon Hall, Great Frieze and Islamic Art collection; Ishtar Gate remains closed until the 2030s.
quote: The Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation announced that the museum will reopen on June 4, 2027. On 4 June 2027, the Pergamon Hall with the Great Frieze, the Collection of Classical Antiquities and the Museum of Islamic Art with the Mshatta façade will be on display again.

claim: Pergamon Museum has been fully closed since October 2023 with the Pergamon Altar wing closed since 2014; full restoration may run until 2037-2043.
quote: The Pergamon Museum has been closed altogether since October 2023... the part of the building containing the Pergamon Altar has been closed for far longer, since 2014.

claim: The Museum Pass Berlin costs €32 (€16 reduced) and covers 30+ museums including all Staatliche Museen and the Jewish Museum on three consecutive calendar days.
quote: The Museum Pass Berlin is a ticket with which you can visit over 30 museums on three consecutive days, including all venues of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin as well as many other museums in Berlin.

claim: Museum Pass is valid for permanent exhibitions only; selected special exhibitions still require an extra time-slot ticket.
quote: The Museum Pass is valid for the museum's permanent exhibition. However, for selected special exhibitions, an additional, fee-based (time-slot) ticket is offered.

claim: All Staatliche Museen zu Berlin venues — including Museum Island museums and Hamburger Bahnhof — are closed on Mondays.
quote: On Mondays, the National Museums in Berlin are closed.

claim: Neues Museum opens Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun 10:00-18:00 and Thu 10:00-20:00; Bode and Altes are also closed Tuesdays in 2026.
quote: Open Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm, and Thursday from 10:00 am to 8:00 pm; closed Mondays.

claim: Jewish Museum Berlin is open Tue-Sun 10-18; the core exhibition in the Libeskind Building is free with online time-slot booking available.
quote: Admission to the core exhibition is free of charge for everyone. Except for certain temporary exhibitions, all other presentations in the Libeskind Building are also free.

claim: A special exhibition 'Between the Lines: Daniel Libeskind and the Jewish Museum Berlin' runs 7 May - 1 Nov 2026.
quote: A special exhibition titled 'Daniel Libeskind and the Jewish Museum Berlin' runs from 7 May to 1 Nov 2026

claim: Hamburger Bahnhof opens Tue/Wed/Fri 10-18, Thu 10-20, Sat-Sun 11-18 and is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026 with eight new exhibitions.
quote: Hours: Tuesday–Wednesday and Friday 10am–6pm, Thursday 10am–8pm, Saturday–Sunday 11am–6pm

claim: Hamburger Bahnhof's 2026 line-up includes Giulia Andreani, Shilpa Gupta, a CHANEL Commission by Lina Lapelytė, and a Ryuichi Sakamoto retrospective opening September 11.
quote: Giulia Andreani (February 27–September 13, 2026)... Shilpa Gupta (March 27, 2026–January 3, 2027)... CHANEL Commission: Lina Lapelytė (May 1, 2026–January 10, 2027)... Ryuichi Sakamoto (September 11, 2026–June 23, 2027)

claim: Berlinische Galerie is open Wed-Mon 10-18 (closed Tuesdays) with €12 entry, €7 reduced, and €7 flat on the first Wednesday of every month.
quote: Admission is €12, reduced €7, and free for visitors up to 18 years of age. Additionally, admission is €7.00 for all on the 1st Wednesday of every month.

claim: Berlinische Galerie's 2026 programme includes Marc Brandenburg, an Emilio Vedova Berlin Diary, Josef Kaiser 'Building for the GDR' and Lovis Corinth 'Then came Berlin!'.
quote: Marc Brandenburg - 20th Century Debris (April 17-September 14, 2026), Emilio Vedova - Absurd Berlin Diary '64... Lovis Corinth - Then came Berlin! (October 9, 2026-January 25, 2027)

claim: DDR Museum is open daily 9:00-21:00 year round (closing 16:00 on Dec 24 and 31), with €13.50 adult tickets, and is one of the most-visited and best-rated interactive museums in Berlin.
quote: The DDR Museum is open every day from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, except on December 24 and 31, when it closes at 4:00 PM. The museum is open daily 365 days a year.

claim: Humboldt Forum opens Mon and Wed-Sun 10:30-18:30 (closed Tuesdays); €14 day ticket covers the Ethnological Museum, Museum of Asian Art and Berlin Global, with several free areas.
quote: A day ticket costs €14 (€7 reduced) and covers all paid exhibitions including the Ethnological Museum, Museum of Asian Art, BERLIN GLOBAL, and temporary exhibitions.

claim: Topography of Terror is open daily 10:00-20:00 with free admission and no time-slot ticket required.
quote: Admission is free. You do not need a time-slot ticket.

claim: While the Pergamon is shut, Yadegar Asisi's 360° 'Pergamonmuseum. Das Panorama' across the canal at Am Kupfergraben 2 costs €12 (€6 reduced) and displays roughly 80 original sculptures including the Telephos Frieze.
quote: the official museum website lists Das Panorama at 12.00 EUR, with concessions at 6.00 EUR

claim: Stasi Museum (Lichtenberg HQ) opens Mon-Fri 10-18 and Sat-Sun 11-18; €6 adult admission with Mielke's preserved office as the headline highlight.
quote: Admission prices are 6 Euros for adults, 4.50 Euros for reduced... A particular highlight is Mielke's office, which has been preserved in its original state

claim: James-Simon-Galerie is the Museum Island visitor centre and main entrance; the Museumsinsel day pass is €24 (€12 reduced) versus €14 per individual museum.
quote: Individual museum tickets are €14 per museum (€7 reduced). The Museum Island day pass (Museumsinsel-Ticket) is €24 (€12 reduced) and covers all museums on the island for one day.

claim: Alte Nationalgalerie's flagship 2026 exhibition on art dealer Paul Cassirer brings 100+ French Impressionist masterpieces (Monet, Degas, Cézanne, van Gogh) to Museum Island May-September 2026.
quote: a major special exhibition in 2026 dedicated to legendary art dealer Paul Cassirer, featuring over 100 masterpieces of French Impressionism — works by Monet, Degas, Cézanne, and van Gogh — running from May to September 2026.
